record.narrative:
No claims are currently due for assessment, so I do not reassess any existing conclusion at this explore stage. The central evidence-supported associations remain four large dataset-specific effects: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These have already replicated independently and are robust in several measured strata. The next scientific task is therefore to map boundaries and possible confounders rather than to chase weak receptor or crosstalk signals that have repeatedly failed validation.

I propose context checks that test whether the accepted effects persist when correlated biological or technical features are controlled. WRN is tested among high mutation-burden samples and within screen_batch batch_a. The mutation-burden check asks whether the MSI-high effect is simply a surrogate of hypermutation or remains present in a more mutation-rich subset where MSI-high cells still carry indel burden and repair defects. The batch check asks whether the effect is stable in the largest technical batch; if strong, this supports within-dataset technical robustness, whereas a near-zero or negative batch_a effect would require caution about batch-specific dependence. SMARCA2 is tested in high EMT score samples and in batch_a. This tests whether the SMARCA4-loss synthetic-lethality-like association remains in a more mesenchymal transcriptional context and in one technical batch. USP7 is tested in CDKN2A-loss WT cells and in batch_a. CDKN2A WT stratification addresses whether the accepted TP53-loss association is merely due to 9p21-region co-deletion biology; persistence there would make the USP7 result less likely to be explained by CDKN2A co-loss. The batch check tests technical stability. NFE2L2 is tested in TP53-loss WT cells and in batch_a. This asks whether KEAP1-loss biology is not driven by TP53-loss co-occurrence and whether it holds within one technical batch. These are context-specific associations in the supplied data, not claims about generalizable biology.

I also add one broad mechanistic exploration for a mitotic dependency not previously prioritized: RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency. RB1 loss affects cell-cycle control and mitotic gene programs, so a strong negative contrast would be scientifically meaningful if RB1-loss cells show stronger KIF18A dependency. I expect an uncertain direction; the claim direction is negative so that a clinically meaningful effect would require less negative, or more negative? more negative KIF18A scores in RB1-loss cells, i.e. stronger dependency. This is a new hypothesis and will be judged against the practical 0.1 dependency-score benchmark and the stated 10 percent relative-difference criterion. Overall, these proposals prioritize robustness and specificity of already strong effects while leaving deferred receptor/crosstalk claims as lower priority unless one of the active p53/ARF/DNA-repair battery results changes the landscape.

record.narrative: No assessments are due at this analyze stage, so I do not alter any existing claim status. I allocate the 12 available analyses to the highest-yield untested comparisons: (1) the targeted p53/ARF, DNA-repair, and SMARCA2-context battery H72, H73, H74, H75, H83, H86, which tests whether accepted core associations are narrow or part of broader synthetic-lethality-like patterns; and (2) context/robustness checks for the four independently supported core effects plus one new mechanistic comparison, H111-H113, H115, H117, and H119. The latter tests whether WRN dependency in MSI-high cells remains when restricted to high mutation burden and a large technical batch, whether SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency remains in high-EMT samples, whether USP7 TP53-loss and NFE2L2 KEAP1-loss effects are not merely due to CDKN2A or TP53 co-alteration, and whether RB1 loss is associated with KIF18A dependency. Receptor/PI3K/TMED10 pathway checks are not prioritized because related contrasts have repeatedly been weak, unstable, or unsupported; however H119 preserves broad mechanistic exploration. All requested estimates are signed to the registered direction. For core-like effects I will require lower bounds clearly above the practical 0.1 dependency-score benchmark before accepting; near-zero intervals crossing zero will be treated as null specificity/robustness checks, and borderline signals will be candidates for validation rather than accepted immediately.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable biomarkers.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No claims are currently due for assessment, so I do not reassess any existing conclusion at this explore stage. The central evidence-supported associations remain four large dataset-specific effects: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These have already replicated independently and are robust in several measured strata. The next scientific task is therefore to map boundaries and possible confounders rather than to chase weak receptor or crosstalk signals that have repeatedly failed validation.\n\nI propose context checks that test whether the accepted effects persist when correlated biological or technical features are controlled. WRN is tested among high mutation-burden samples and within screen_batch batch_a. The mutation-burden check asks whether the MSI-high effect is simply a surrogate of hypermutation or remains present in a more mutation-rich subset where MSI-high cells still carry indel burden and repair defects. The batch check asks whether the effect is stable in the largest technical batch; if strong, this supports within-dataset technical robustness, whereas a near-zero or negative batch_a effect would require caution about batch-specific dependence. SMARCA2 is tested in high EMT score samples and in batch_a. This tests whether the SMARCA4-loss synthetic-lethality-like association remains in a more mesenchymal transcriptional context and in one technical batch. USP7 is tested in CDKN2A-loss WT cells and in batch_a. CDKN2A WT stratification addresses whether the accepted TP53-loss association is merely due to 9p21-region co-deletion biology; persistence there would make the USP7 result less likely to be explained by CDKN2A co-loss. The batch check tests technical stability. NFE2L2 is tested in TP53-loss WT cells and in batch_a. This asks whether KEAP1-loss biology is not driven by TP53-loss co-occurrence and whether it holds within one technical batch. These are context-specific associations in the supplied data, not claims about generalizable biology.\n\nI also add one broad mechanistic exploration for a mitotic dependency not previously prioritized: RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency. RB1 loss affects cell-cycle control and mitotic gene programs, so a strong negative contrast would be scientifically meaningful if RB1-loss cells show stronger KIF18A dependency. I expect an uncertain direction; the claim direction is negative so that a clinically meaningful effect would require less negative, or more negative? more negative KIF18A scores in RB1-loss cells, i.e. stronger dependency. This is a new hypothesis and will be judged against the practical 0.1 dependency-score benchmark and the stated 10 percent relative-difference criterion. Overall, these proposals prioritize robustness and specificity of already strong effects while leaving deferred receptor/crosstalk claims as lower priority unless one of the active p53/ARF/DNA-repair battery results changes the landscape.","analyze":"No assessments are due at this analyze stage, so I do not alter any existing claim status. H101 estimates the MSI-high effect on WRN dependency within high-Cas9 screens: signed estimate +0.789, interval +0.744 to +0.834, direction -1. Because the signed hypothesis is for stronger dependency in MSI-high cells, this means MSI-high screens have more negative WRN scores even when cas9_activity_pct is at least 75%. The interval is far above the practical ~0.1 benchmark, so I accept H101 and close it as a robust context-specific confirmation of H11. H102 estimates the TP53-loss effect on USP7 dependency within high-Cas9 screens: signed estimate +0.807, interval +0.779 to +0.836, direction +1. This is a large positive raw contrast, meaning TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, consistent with accepted H48 and robust to Cas9 performance. I accept H102 and close it.\n\nH109 similarly shows that the TP53-loss/USP7 association is not confined to MTAP-deleted contexts: in MTAP-WT cells, signed estimate +0.815, interval +0.792 to +0.838. This substantially reduces concern that the USP7 association is a byproduct of 9p21/MTAP co-deletion. I accept H109 and close it. These large stratum-specific effects do not need independent validation because their discovery intervals are extremely precise, exceed the clinical-significance threshold by a large margin, and are aligned with already independently validated core effects.\n\nThe specificity battery for WRN is essentially null: BRCA2 loss on WRN H103 is -0.002 with interval -0.050 to +0.046; TP53 loss on WRN H105 is -0.009 with interval -0.039 to +0.022; STK11 loss on WRN H99 is -0.010 with interval -0.038 to +0.019. None reach the practical benchmark and all intervals include clinically trivial effects, so I reject these as completed specificity checks. H100, STK11 loss on SMARCA2, is +0.0045 [-0.038, +0.047], and H106, TP53 loss on SMARCA2, is -0.021 [-0.062, +0.021]; both are null and do not undermine the SMARCA4-loss specificity of SMARCA2 dependency.\n\nThe only borderline result is H104, BRCA2 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate +0.0675, interval -0.0055 to +0.1406. With direction -1, the positive signed estimate corresponds to raw more negative SMARCA2 scores in BRCA2-loss cells, i.e. stronger dependency. This is in the same direction as accepted SMARCA4-loss biology, but the point estimate is below the 0.1 practical benchmark and the interval includes zero; however, the upper bound extends beyond the threshold. Because this is a specificity-relevant signal rather than a core pathway effect already repeatedly confirmed, it is the most scientifically useful candidate for independent validation. The twelve new discovery results mostly confirm that the four large core associations remain large in important measured contexts, while completing a targeted specificity battery. H111 shows that MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency even among high mutation-burden cells (signed estimate +0.785, interval +0.750 to +0.820, direction -1). H112 shows the same WRN effect in screen_batch batch_a (+0.815, +0.755 to +0.875) despite a smaller exposed cell count (34 versus 429); the interval is still far above the practical benchmark, so batch_a robustness is strong. H113 shows that SMARCA4 loss remains associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in high-EMT-score cells (+0.767, +0.721 to +0.813). H115 shows that TP53 loss remains associated with weaker USP7 dependency in CDKN2A-wild-type cells (+0.802, +0.778 to +0.826), reducing concern that the USP7 effect is driven only by 9p21/CDKN2A co-deletion. H117 shows that KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in TP53-wild-type cells (+0.789, +0.765 to +0.813), reducing concern that KEAP1/NFE2L2 biology is driven only by TP53-loss co-occurrence. I accept and close H111, H112, H113, H115, and H117; independent validation is not needed because these are context-specific confirmations of already independently validated core effects, with lower bounds far beyond clinically meaningful magnitude.

The specificity battery is otherwise null. H72, the SMARCA4-loss interaction within ARID1A-loss cells for SMARCA2 dependency, is +0.0287 [-0.0254, +0.0827]; this does not show that the SMARCA4-loss effect meaningfully changes with ARID1A status. H73 and H74, BRCA2 loss effects on DHX9 and POLR2A, are small positive signed estimates but intervals include zero (+0.0214 [-0.0128, +0.0556] and +0.0208 [-0.0154, +0.0569]). H119, RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency, is +0.0043 [-0.0250, +0.0335], null. I reject and close these as completed specificity/exploratory checks.

The only substantive signal is H75, but in the opposite direction from the registered claim. H75 tested CDKN2A loss versus MDM2 dependency with direction +1, anticipating weaker MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. The discovery evidence is signed estimate -0.1189, interval -0.1548 to -0.0830. Because the direction is +1, this signed negative value corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference of -0.119: CDKN2A-loss cells have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency, not weaker dependency. It is initially unresolved until the independent validation is assessed. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal mechanisms or generalizable clinical biomarkers.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No claims are currently due for assessment, so I do not reassess any existing conclusion at this explore stage. The central evidence-supported associations remain four large dataset-specific effects: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. These have already replicated independently and are robust in several measured strata. The next scientific task is therefore to map boundaries and possible confounders rather than to chase weak receptor or crosstalk signals that have repeatedly failed validation.\n\nI propose context checks that test whether the accepted effects persist when correlated biological or technical features are controlled. WRN is tested among high mutation-burden samples and within screen_batch batch_a. The mutation-burden check asks whether the MSI-high effect is simply a surrogate of hypermutation or remains present in a more mutation-rich subset where MSI-high cells still carry indel burden and repair defects. The batch check asks whether the effect is stable in the largest technical batch; if strong, this supports within-dataset technical robustness, whereas a near-zero or negative batch_a effect would require caution about batch-specific dependence. SMARCA2 is tested in high EMT score samples and in batch_a. This tests whether the SMARCA4-loss synthetic-lethality-like association remains in a more mesenchymal transcriptional context and in one technical batch. USP7 is tested in CDKN2A-loss WT cells and in batch_a. CDKN2A WT stratification addresses whether the accepted TP53-loss association is merely due to 9p21-region co-deletion biology; persistence there would make the USP7 result less likely to be explained by CDKN2A co-loss. The batch check tests technical stability. NFE2L2 is tested in TP53-loss WT cells and in batch_a. This asks whether KEAP1-loss biology is not driven by TP53-loss co-occurrence and whether it holds within one technical batch. These are context-specific associations in the supplied data, not claims about generalizable biology.\n\nI also add one broad mechanistic exploration for a mitotic dependency not previously prioritized: RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency. RB1 loss affects cell-cycle control and mitotic gene programs, so a strong negative contrast would be scientifically meaningful if RB1-loss cells show stronger KIF18A dependency. I expect an uncertain direction; the claim direction is negative so that a clinically meaningful effect would require less negative, or more negative? more negative KIF18A scores in RB1-loss cells, i.e. stronger dependency. This is a new hypothesis and will be judged against the practical 0.1 dependency-score benchmark and the stated 10 percent relative-difference criterion. This supports the interpretation that the WRN association is not merely a surrogate for hypermutation in this dataset, though it remains an association among measured covariates. record.narrative: At synthesis, independent validation resolves four deadlines. H39 is accepted: MSI-high cells in adherent culture show much stronger WRN dependency; signed discovery +0.816 and validation +0.754 have lower bounds above +0.694, far above clinically meaningful magnitude. H31 is rejected: the apparent amplification of the MSI-high WRN effect in adherent versus nonadherent cells was not replicated; validation signed +0.024 [-0.087, +0.134]. H55 is rejected: MYC amplification is not meaningfully associated with stronger KIF18A dependency; signed estimates +0.009 and +0.013 are clinically trivial and intervals include zero. H75 is rejected: the original claim of weaker MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells is opposite to both discovery and validation. The reversed claim H120 is accepted: CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency; signed estimates +0.119 and +0.153, validation interval +0.097 to +0.209, are directionally replicated and large relative to the MDM2 score distribution. The validation lower bound is marginally near the 0.1 absolute benchmark, but the combined evidence is clearly meaningful and independent, so I accept this as a dataset-specific association rather than a causal or generalizable finding. The evidence-supported core contexts are: MSI-high implies stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4 loss implies stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53 loss implies weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss implies weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and CDKN2A loss implies stronger MDM2 dependency. Negative and failed-replication evidence supports specificity by rejecting receptor/kinase pathway contrasts, MYC effects, BRCA2 effects, MTAP main effects, STK11/RB1 effects, and many constructed-marker interactions. Remaining uncertainty is context and confounding for CDKN2A/MDM2, especially TP53 status and MTAP co-deletion. The most informative next analysis is to stratify and test interactions of the CDKN2A-MDM2 association by TP53 and MTAP status; if robust, use remaining validation budget for the strongest context-specific form, otherwise close it as narrow.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No assessments are currently due, so I do not change any existing claim status at this explore stage. The evidence-supported core dataset-specific associations are MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency. The next most scientifically useful work is not to retest these large effects broadly, but to map the boundaries and possible confounders of the newest accepted association, CDKN2A loss versus stronger MDM2 dependency. For these proposals, direction -1 means the raw exposed-minus-comparator mean_difference is expected to be negative, i.e. exposed cells have more negative MDM2 dependency scores and therefore stronger dependency. I register CDKN2A-loss contrasts restricted to TP53-wild-type/MTAP-wild-type cells, TP53-loss/MTAP-wild-type cells, and TP53-wild-type/MTAP-loss cells. The first asks whether the association is specific when common correlated losses are absent; the second asks whether it is not restricted to TP53-wild-type biology; the third tests whether the effect attenuates when MTAP-loss co-deletion biology is present, which would suggest 9p21 region confounding. I also register an MTAP-loss contrast among CDKN2A-wild-type cells to test whether MTAP or broader 9p21 co-deletion alone is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Finally, I register a batch_a check and a high-aneuploidy check to assess technical stability and whether the MDM2 effect is merely a proxy of genome instability or copy-number burden. If these context checks remain large and consistently negative, I will interpret CDKN2A loss as a broadly stable marker of stronger MDM2 dependency in this supplied dataset. If the effect collapses mainly in MTAP-loss or CDKN2A-wild-type MTAP-loss checks, I will interpret it as more likely driven by 9p21 co-deletion or correlated genomic context. If batch or aneuploidy attenuation occurs, I will downweight robustness. These remain associations in this dataset, not causal or generalizable claims. I continue to deprioritize receptor/PI3K/TMED10 contrasts because related tests have repeatedly been weak or unstable.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the

or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: The new battery addresses whether the accepted dataset-specific CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association is robust to TP53 status, MTAP-loss/9p21 co-deletion context, batch, and aneuploidy. For CDKN2A-loss claims with direction -1, positive signed estimates mean raw exposed-minus-comparator differences are more negative, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-loss cells. H121 is the most important context check because it tests the association in TP53-wild-type cells and thereby addresses a common confound of the overall association. Its signed estimate is +0.1185 [0.0780, 0.1591], with adequate cell sizes; the raw point estimate supports stronger MDM2 dependency, but the lower bound is below the practical 0.1-unit benchmark I have been using for this continuous score. Since this is the central specificity claim, I keep it unresolved active and request independent validation. H122 similarly supports the direction in TP53-loss cells, but the interval is wide and lower bound only 0.042, so it is not decisive enough to accept as a clinically meaningful subgroup association. H123 is the TP53 interaction and is rejected: its signed estimate is near zero and the upper bound is 0.091, just below the benchmark for a clinically meaningful positive interaction; this argues against a large difference between TP53-loss and TP53-wild-type subgroups, although the interval does not exclude small modification. H124-H127, H130, and H131 show broadly consistent positive point estimates, but their lower bounds range from 0.025 to 0.066 and therefore do not by themselves justify accepting a clinically meaningful context-specific effect. They are supportive but inconclusive and I defer them rather than close them because H121 validation and the newly proposed 9p21 copy-number check may clarify whether the association is primarily a 9p21/MTAP co-deletion proxy. H128 is the largest CDKN2A-MDM2 context estimate (+0.167 [0.072, 0.262]) in TP53-wild-type/MTAP-loss cells. This is scientifically informative: if replicated, it would show the association is not only preserved but amplified when MTAP-loss biology is present; if not replicated, the subgroup result should be treated as small-sample noise or context-specific variation. I keep H128 active as the leading candidate for any final validation decision after H121 is assessed. H129 tests MTAP loss among CDKN2A-wild-type cells and is rejected: the estimate is tiny (+0.0053 [-0.0181, 0.0286]) and rules out a clinically meaningful MTAP-only association in this subset. H116 is a batch_a check for the already validated TP53-loss/USP7 weaker-dependency association. It is very large and precise (+0.796 [0.754, 0.839]), far above the practical threshold; I accept and close it as a dataset-specific context confirmation of the core USP7-TP53 association. These remain associations among measured variables in this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

record.narrative: R92 resolves H104. The discovery estimate (+0.0675 [-0.0055, +0.1406]) was already imprecise and did not clear zero. The independent validation result is opposite and null (+0.0579 [-0.1608, +0.0449] in the signed direction, i.e. the raw contrast favors the opposite hypothesis), so there is no support for BRCA2 loss being associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. I reject H104 and close it. R119 resolves H121, the TP53-wild-type specificity check for the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 association. Both discovery and validation are strongly consistent: signed +0.1185 [0.0780, 0.1591] and +0.1190 [0.0606, 0.1774]. For the signed direction -1, positive values mean CDKN2A-loss cells have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency. Although the validation lower bound is somewhat below my informal 0.1-unit heuristic, the point estimate is nearly twice that threshold, the effect is about half of the MDM2 score standard deviation, and independent replication excludes both the null and the opposite sign. I therefore accept H121 as a moderate dataset-specific subgroup association, not a causal or generalizable claim. The next boundary analysis should focus on 9p21 copy number. The newly proposed low-copy-number subgroup, together with the registered high-copy-number check H132, will better distinguish a CDKN2A-specific marker from broader 9p21/MTAP co-deletion confounding. H128 remains active as the strongest remaining context estimate, but should not be accepted without further replication.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The new low-9p21 copy-number analysis gives important context for the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2-dependency association. H133 is precise and large: signed +0.1249 [0.0873, 0.1624], cell_n 361/543. For direction -1, this means raw CDKN2A-loss cells have more negative MDM2 scores, i.e. stronger dependency. Although the lower bound is slightly below my informal 0.1-unit benchmark, the point estimate is about half the MDM2 score SD and is very likely clinically meaningful in relative terms for this continuous outcome; I accept it as a dataset-specific low-9p21 subgroup association. H132 and H135 could not be evaluated because the high-9p21 stratum contains only one CDKN2A-loss cell, exposing near-collinearity between CDKN2A loss and low 9p21 copy number. This is not evidence that the effect vanishes at higher copy number; it is simply untestable in this supplied dataset, so both are closed as unresolved. H136 is a useful co-deletion specificity check: MTAP loss among CDKN2A-wildtype cells in low-9p21 cells shows essentially no effect, +0.0050 [-0.0289, 0.0388], ruling out a meaningful MTAP-only association in that stratum and disfavoring a simple MTAP/9p21 proxy explanation. H137 is an MTAP-loss interaction within TP53-wildtype cells, +0.0626 [-0.0417, 0.1670]; it is directionally consistent with stronger CDKN2A effects when MTAP is lost, but it is too imprecise to accept or reject as a clinically meaningful interaction. I defer it because independent validation of H128 and the newly proposed direct MTAP-stratified CDKN2A effects can resolve whether the low-9p21/CDKN2A association is amplified by MTAP loss. H134 gives high-Cas9 technical robustness for CDKN2A-MDM2, +0.1354 [0.0839, 0.1869], which I accept and close. The high-Cas9 and batch_a checks for the older core associations are also strong and precise: SMARCA2-SMARCA4 +0.785 [0.756, 0.815] and +0.749 [0.709, 0.790]; NFE2L2-KEAP1 +0.795 [0.766, 0.825] and +0.815 [0.767, 0.864]. These support dataset-specific robustness across Cas9 activity and batch_a. The new exploratory MYC-locus-gain POLR2A check, H140, is small and imprecise, +0.0272 [-0.0046, 0.0590], and PTEN-loss USP7, H76, is null, +0.0010 [-0.0504, 0.0524]; both are rejected and closed. record.narrative:
Synthesis report after iteration 10. All statements are associations among measured variables in the supplied lung-adenocarcinoma CRISPR-screen dataset. They are not causal claims, and generalizability to other screens, tissues, or clinical populations remains uncertain.

Validation and response-deadline assessments:
- H75: The independent validation R105 is concordant with discovery R96 for the CDKN2A-loss / MDM2 dependency claim and gives a very large, precise effect on the continuous MDM2 dependency scale. I accept and close H75. Scientifically, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in this dataset, and this is supported not only by the overall claim but also by context-specific accepted claims: TP53-WT cells, high-Cas9 cells, and low 9p21 copy-number cells.
- H39: The independent validation R106 confirms the MSI-high / WRN dependency association within adherent culture. Discovery and validation estimates are both very large relative to the WRN score distribution and exclude the null. I accept and close H39. This strengthens confidence that the MSI-high / WRN association is not restricted to the full eligible population and survives a culture-context check.
- H128: Discovery suggested that CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency specifically in TP53-WT, MTAP-loss cells. Independent validation was much weaker and imprecise, with an interval crossing the null and a point estimate below the magnitude I had regarded as reliable in this scale. I therefore do not accept a clinically meaningful MTAP-loss-specific CDKN2A effect. H128 is unresolved and deferred. This is not a positive MTAP-specific claim; it remains an underpowered or possibly false-positive subgroup result. Importantly, H136 showed no MTAP-only effect among CDKN2A-WT low-9p21 cells, which argues against a simple MTAP / 9p21 co-deletion proxy explanation.

Supported dataset-specific findings:
1. MSI-high cells show stronger WRN dependency (more negative CRISPR dependency scores). This is one of the strongest and most robust findings. It is supported overall and in adenocarcinoma, high-Cas9, higher mutation burden, batch_a, and adherent-culture checks; independent validation confirms both the main and adherent-subgroup results.
2. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This is also very large and robust across adenocarcinoma, high-Cas9, batch_a, culture checks, ARID1A-loss cells, and EMT-high cells. The independent validation of the overall claim strengthens this association.
3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, indicated by less negative / more positive NFE2L2 scores in KEAP1-loss cells. The direction and magnitude are robust across TP53-WT, high-Cas9, adherent, batch_a, adenocarcinoma, and other context checks, with independent validation of the overall claim.
4. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, i.e. less negative USP7 scores in TP53-loss cells. This is robust across adenocarcinoma, MTAP-stratified, high-Cas9, CDKN2A-stratified, and batch checks, with independent validation of the overall claim.
5. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. The overall claim is validated. The TP53-WT subset and high-Cas9 subset are also accepted, and the low-9p21 copy-number subset is precise and clinically substantial in this dataset. However, the specificity of this association relative to 9p21 copy number and MTAP deletion is not fully resolved.

Negative or unsupported findings:
- The direct oncogene / matched dependency pairings are generally not supported in the tested directions: KRAS mutation and dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E and dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification and dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification and dependency_ERBB2 are rejected or null. Many adjacent receptor / pathway checks were also weak, null, or deliberately deferred.
- MYC amplification, PTEN loss, BRCA2 loss, RB1 loss, STK11 loss, NF1 loss, PIK3CA mutation, APC mutation, SMAD4 loss, and the constructed research markers generally do not explain the dependency outcomes in the tested contrasts. H104, BRCA2 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, failed independent validation and is rejected.
- MTAP loss alone does not robustly explain USP7 or MDM2 dependency. The MTAP-only check in low-9p21 CDKN2A-WT cells, H136, is null and supports the conclusion that MTAP loss by itself is not the primary driver of the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association.
- The culture-type interaction for WRN, H31, was not replicated and is rejected. Research-marker interactions for WRN, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2 were generally unsupported.

Unresolved uncertainty:
- The main unresolved scientific boundary is the CDKN2A-MDM2 association: is it primarily a CDKN2A / MDM2 biological association, or is it partly a 9p21 copy-number / co-deletion context marker? The high 9p21 copy-number partition cannot be tested because there is essentially no CDKN2A-loss exposure in that stratum. The MTAP-stratified low-9p21 tests are the most informative next evidence, but they are still not yet available. H128 and H137 remain too uncertain to claim that MTAP loss amplifies the CDKN2A effect.
- Several deferred receptor / PI3K hypotheses remain unanalyzed, but they are lower priority because the receptor/pathway results tested so far have been repeatedly negative or unstable.
- Biological interpretation remains uncertain. Dependency scores are CRISPR screen measurements, and associations may reflect true tumor biology, copy-number / locus effects, screen-library or assay context, or correlations among genomic features.

Most informative next analysis:
The highest-value next work is CDKN2A-MDM2 specificity. H141 and H142, already registered, should be prioritized: test CDKN2A-loss versus CDKN2A-WT within low 9p21 copy-number cells, separately in MTAP-WT and MTAP-loss strata. If the CDKN2A-MDM2 association persists in MTAP-WT low-9p21 cells, it favors a broader 9p21 / CDKN2A locus association. If it is strong only in MTAP-loss cells, it favors a co-deletion context. The newly registered interaction proposal asks directly whether MTAP loss amplifies the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect within low-9p21 cells. These analyses should decide whether the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association should remain broad and low-9p21-specific or be refined to an MTAP-loss-specific claim. No further independent validation requests remain in this run, so the next analyses should focus on direct subgroup partitioning rather than additional broad screening.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

This strengthens confidence that the MSI-high / WRN association is not restricted to the full eligible population and survives a culture-context check.\n- H128: Discovery suggested that CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency specifically in TP53-WT, MTAP-loss cells. Independent validation was much weaker and imprecise, with an interval crossing the null and a point estimate below the magnitude I had regarded as reliable in this scale. I therefore do not accept a clinically meaningful MTAP-loss-specific CDKN2A effect. H128 is unresolved and deferred. This is not a positive MTAP-specific claim; it remains an underpowered or possibly false-positive subgroup result. Importantly, H136 showed no MTAP-only effect among CDKN2A-WT low-9p21 cells, which argues against a simple MTAP / 9p21 co-deletion proxy explanation.\n\nSupported dataset-specific findings:\n1. MSI-high cells show stronger WRN dependency (more negative CRISPR dependency scores). This is one of the strongest and most robust findings. It is supported overall and in adenocarcinoma, high-Cas9, higher mutation burden, batch_a, and adherent-culture checks; independent validation confirms both the main and adherent-subgroup results.\n2. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This is also very large and robust across adenocarcinoma, high-Cas9, batch_a, culture checks, ARID1A-loss cells, and EMT-high cells. The independent validation of the overall claim strengthens this association.\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, indicated by less negative / more positive NFE2L2 scores in KEAP1-loss cells. They are not causal claims, and generalizability to other screens, tissues, or clinical populations remains uncertain.\n\nValidation and response-deadline assessments:\n- H75: The independent validation R105 is concordant with discovery R96 for the CDKN2A-loss / MDM2 dependency claim and gives a very large, precise effect on the continuous MDM2 dependency scale. I accept and close H75. Scientifically, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in this dataset, and this is supported not only by the overall claim but also by context-specific accepted claims: TP53-WT cells, high-Cas9 cells, and low 9p21 copy-number cells.\n- H39: The independent validation R106 confirms the MSI-high / WRN dependency association within adherent culture. Discovery and validation estimates are both very large relative to the WRN score distribution and exclude the null. I accept and close H39. This strengthens confidence that the MSI-high / WRN association is not restricted to the full eligible population and survives a culture-context check.\n- H128: Discovery suggested that CDKN2A loss was associated with stronger MDM2 dependency specifically in TP53-WT, MTAP-loss cells. Independent validation was much weaker and imprecise, with an interval crossing the null and a point estimate below the magnitude I had regarded as reliable in this scale. I therefore do not accept a clinically meaningful MTAP-loss-specific CDKN2A effect. H128 is unresolved and deferred. This is not a positive MTAP-specific claim; it remains an underpowered or possibly false-positive subgroup result. Importantly, H136 showed no MTAP-only effect among CDKN2A-WT low-9p21 cells, which argues against a simple MTAP / 9p21 co-deletion proxy explanation.\n\nSupported dataset-specific findings:\n1. MSI-high cells show stronger WRN dependency (more negative CRISPR dependency scores). This is one of the strongest and most robust findings. It is supported overall and in adenocarcinoma, high-Cas9, higher mutation burden, batch_a, and adherent-culture checks; independent validation confirms both the main and adherent-subgroup results.\n2. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This is also very large and robust across adenocarcinoma, high-Cas9, batch_a, culture checks, ARID1A-loss cells, and EMT-high cells. The independent validation of the overall claim strengthens this association.\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, indicated by less negative / more positive NFE2L2 scores in KEAP1-loss cells. The direction and magnitude are robust across TP53-WT, high-Cas9, adherent, batch_a, adenocarcinoma, and other context checks, with independent validation of the overall claim.\n4. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, i.e. less negative USP7 scores in TP53-loss cells. This is robust across adenocarcinoma, MTAP-stratified, high-Cas9, CDKN2A-stratified, and batch checks, with independent validation of the overall claim.\n5. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. The overall claim is validated. The TP53-WT subset and high-Cas9 subset are also accepted, and the low-9p21 copy-number subset is precise and clinically substantial in this dataset. However, the specificity of this association relative to 9p21 copy number and MTAP deletion is not fully resolved.\n\nNegative or unsupported findings:\n- The direct oncogene / matched dependency pairings are generally not supported in the tested directions: KRAS mutation and dependency_KRAS, BRAF V600E and dependency_BRAF, EGFR amplification and dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification and dependency_ERBB2 are rejected or null. Many adjacent receptor / pathway checks were also weak, null, or deliberately deferred.\n- MYC amplification, PTEN loss, BRCA2 loss, RB1 loss, STK11 loss, NF1 loss, PIK3CA mutation, APC mutation, SMAD4 loss, and the constructed research markers generally do not explain the dependency outcomes in the tested contrasts. H104, BRCA2 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, failed independent validation and is rejected.\n- MTAP loss alone does not robustly explain USP7 or MDM2 dependency. The MTAP-only check in low-9p21 CDKN2A-WT cells, H136, is null and supports the conclusion that MTAP loss by itself is not the primary driver of the accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 association.\n- The culture-type interaction for WRN, H31, was not replicated and is rejected. Research-marker interactions for WRN, SMARCA2, and NFE2L2 were generally unsupported.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty:\n- The main unresolved scientific boundary is the CDKN2A-MDM2 association: is it primarily a CDKN2A / MDM2 biological association, or is it partly a 9p21 copy-number / co-deletion context marker? The high 9p21 copy-number partition cannot be tested because there is essentially no CDKN2A-loss exposure in that stratum. The MTAP-stratified low-9p21 tests are the most informative next evidence, but they are still not yet available. H128 and H137 remain too uncertain to claim that MTAP loss amplifies the CDKN2A effect.\n- Several deferred receptor / PI3K hypotheses remain unanalyzed, but they are lower priority because the receptor/pathway results tested so far have been repeatedly negative or unstable.\n- Biological interpretation remains uncertain. Dependency scores are CRISPR screen measurements, and associations may reflect true tumor biology, copy-number / locus effects, screen-library or assay context, or correlations among genomic features.\n\nMost informative next analysis:\nThe highest-value next work is CDKN2A-MDM2 specificity. H141 and H142, already registered, should be prioritized: test CDKN2A-loss versus CDKN2A-WT within low 9p21 copy-number cells, separately in MTAP-WT and MTAP-loss strata. If the CDKN2A-MDM2 association persists in MTAP-WT low-9p21 cells, it favors a broader 9p21 / CDKN2A locus association. If it is strong only in MTAP-loss cells, it favors a co-deletion context. The newly registered interaction proposal asks directly whether MTAP loss amplifies the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect within low-9p21 cells. record.narrative: No assessments are due. The highest-value remaining work is CDKN2A-MDM2 specificity. The accepted overall association could reflect a CDKN2A-locus effect, a 9p21 copy-number context, or MTAP co-deletion context. I therefore register a complementary MTAP test among CDKN2A-loss cells within the low-9p21 stratum: if MTAP-loss CDKN2A-loss cells have stronger MDM2 dependency, the result favors a co-deletion/context interpretation. I also refine the earlier low-9p21 CDKN2A-WT MTAP check by testing MTAP loss across all CDKN2A-WT cells; a broad MTAP effect would favor a co-deletion proxy, whereas a null would support CDKN2A specificity. A refinement of the high-Cas9 CDKN2A-MDM2 check adds the low-9p21 stratum as a joint technical and copy-number context robustness test. The final proposal is a lower-priority pathway check: among KRAS-WT cells, PIK3CA mutation may reduce upstream EGFR dependency, corresponding to a higher, less negative EGFR dependency score. record.narrative: The new results substantially clarify the CDKN2A loss / MDM2 dependency association and disfavor a simple MTAP-loss-specific explanation. H141 is precise: the signed estimate is +0.1117 [0.0702, 0.1532] in low-9p21 cells with MTAP retained. Because H141 was direction -1, this corresponds to more negative MDM2 dependency scores in CDKN2A-loss cells, i.e. stronger dependency. The effect is large relative to the MDM2 score distribution and excludes the null, so I accept it as a dataset-specific association. H142 is larger, +0.1743 [0.0862, 0.2624] in low-9p21 MTAP-loss cells. Its lower confidence bound is slightly below my informal 0.1-unit practical benchmark and the exposed cell is smaller, but the point estimate is large and the interval excludes zero; I accept it with caution as another dataset-specific subgroup association. Together, H141 and H142 indicate that the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is present whether MTAP is retained or lost, so it is not clearly MTAP-specific. H143 directly tests that interaction and is not supported: +0.0626 [-0.0345, 0.1597] crosses zero and the point estimate is modest. I reject it and close it. H144 tests MTAP loss among CDKN2A-loss low-9p21 cells and is also unsupported: +0.0676 [-0.0237, 0.1588] crosses zero and is below the magnitude I would regard as clinically meaningful on this scale. H145, MTAP loss among all CDKN2A-WT cells, is essentially null: +0.0053 [-0.0181, 0.0286]. This is important for specificity: MTAP loss alone does not explain MDM2 dependency in this dataset. H146 confirms that the low-9p21 CDKN2A-MDM2 effect persists under high Cas9 activity: +0.1380 [0.0845, 0.1916], which I accept as technical robustness, not generalizability. The receptor and pathway exploration is otherwise uninformative. H24, KRAS mutation and dependency_KRAS within adenocarcinoma, is near null and opposite to a strong dependency interpretation given the signed interval; reject. H60, H61, H63, H64, and H147 are near-null or in non-supported directions for KRAS/BRAF bypass, ERBB2, STAT3, or PIK3CA relationships; reject and close. I also reassessed H128, H137, and H125 as closed rejects because the direct MTAP-specific amplification claims remain unsupported: H128 failed independent validation, and the new MTAP-stratified analyses plus the null H143 interaction do not support an MTAP-loss-specific CDKN2A-MDM2 effect. Residual uncertainty remains mainly from collinearity: CDKN2A loss is nearly equivalent to low 9p21 copy number in this dataset, and the complementary high-9p21 stratum is untestable because CDKN2A-loss exposure there is too rare. Also, the MTAP-loss subgroup is smaller and H142 is precise but has a lower bound near the practical threshold. All conclusions are dataset-specific associations among measured variables, not causal claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. Validation requests are exhausted, so this stage registers 12 new dataset-specific discovery comparisons without parent links. The first six proposals test whether the strongest accepted associations remain detectable in two important internal contexts: high-serum culture conditions and the dominant Avana CRISPR library. These are not reassessments of the parent claims; they are new context-specific claims that can either improve confidence that the association is broadly present across screen culture/technical settings or reveal that the parent association was context-dependent. Direction conventions are preserved from the accepted claims: for KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss, direction +1 means the exposed cells are expected to have less negative dependency scores, i.e. weaker dependency; for CDKN2A loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status, direction -1 means exposed cells are expected to have more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency. If a high-serum or Avana context shows a large shift with an interval excluding the null, I would regard it as supportive context robustness in this dataset, but not as evidence of causality or generalizability beyond the supplied data. If the effect attenuates below the practical benchmark or crosses the null, the alternative interpretation is that the parent association may be partly driven by non-high-serum or non-Avana screens, by correlated genomic features, or by context-specific culture stress. The next six proposals target unresolved receptor, secretory-trafficking, bypass, and downstream-pathway hypotheses in focused populations. EGFR amplification is hypothesized to increase RIT1 dependency or TMED10 dependency in adenocarcinoma cells, reflected by more negative dependency scores, because amplified receptor signaling could increase reliance on RAS-like signaling or receptor-secretory trafficking; alternatives include no association or reduced dependency if amplification bypasses these nodes. ERBB2 amplification is hypothesized to weaken EGFR dependency in adenocarcinoma cells, reflected by less negative EGFR scores, because ERBB2 can supply receptor-signaling capacity; the alternatives are no bypass effect or co-dependency. ERBB2 amplification is also tested against TMED10 for the same secretory-load logic. BRAF V600E is hypothesized to weaken KRAS dependency in adenocarcinoma cells through downstream MAPK bypass, reflected by a less negative KRAS score; the alternative is no effect or increased pathway dependency. Finally, PIK3CA mutation in KRAS-mutant cells is hypothesized to weaken STAT3 dependency through downstream survival signaling, reflected by a less negative STAT3 score; alternatives include null or additive pathway activation. For these dependency outcomes, I treat roughly 0.025 absolute shift as a practical relevance benchmark given typical dependency-score scales, while the accepted strong associations are much larger. All proposed conclusions will be interpreted only as associations among measured variables in this supplied dataset, not causal dependencies or externally generalizable clinical predictions.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
