status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I interpreted all returned estimates as already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 mean-difference claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative, stronger dependency score; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative, weaker dependency score; for interaction claims, a positive signed estimate means the registered exposed-minus-comparator contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. H268 accepts as a within-dataset PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association in PIK3CA-mutant cells: the signed difference is +0.261, 95% CI 0.118 to 0.403, with 36 exposed and 273 comparator cells. The effect is large relative to the STAT3 dependency distribution, but the exposed cell count is modest and the subgroup was tested after selection on PIK3CA state, so I keep it deferred rather than closed because PTEN-STAT3 remains discovery-only and may be confounded by PI3K-pathway and genomic context. H269 similarly accepts a PTEN-loss/STAT3 association among TP53-loss cells: +0.198, 95% CI 0.089 to 0.307, n 52/309. This is somewhat smaller than the main PTEN effect but still imprecisely positive and biologically plausible; it remains deferred as an unvalidated within-dataset context check. H270 rejects the claim of a positive high-aneuploidy interaction modifying PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency: the signed interaction is -0.089, 95% CI -0.215 to 0.037. The point estimate is opposite the registered direction and the interval is too wide to support a meaningful positive interaction. This is not a claim that high aneuploidy has no effect; rather, this dataset provides no evidence for the specific claimed positive modification. H271 accepts a large PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in high IFN-gamma signature cells: +0.458, 95% CI 0.345 to 0.570, n 59/384. The magnitude is much larger than the overall PTEN-STAT3 effect and the interval excludes zero comfortably. However, the subgroup was defined by a continuous assay and PTEN loss may co-occur with inflammatory or lineage states, so I accept it as an internally supported but deferred context finding, not a causal or generalized result. H272 rejects ARID1A-loss association with SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-intact cells: +0.002, 95% CI -0.021 to 0.026. This is essentially null and inconsistent with the paralog-compensation hypothesis. H273-H277 are accepted as confirmatory context checks of previously supported core associations. H273 shows TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency among KEAP1-loss cells: +0.791, 95% CI 0.750 to 0.832, n 74/276. H274 shows KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency among TP53-loss cells: +0.828, 95% CI 0.778 to 0.878, n 74/287. H275 shows MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency among faster-growing cells: +0.776, 95% CI 0.733 to 0.820, n 58/719. H276 shows CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency among STK11-loss cells: +0.111, 95% CI 0.038 to 0.184, n 63/276; the interval is less expansive than the main validated CDKN2A-MDM2 effect but remains positive and consistent. H277 shows SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in high-stemness cells: +0.789, 95% CI 0.749 to 0.830, n 91/362. These effects are large, precise, and consistent with earlier accepted and validated findings, though they remain associations within overlapping discovery samples. H278 rejects MYC amplification as a predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency: -0.008, 95% CI -0.040 to 0.025, with a null-to-negligible signed effect. H279 rejects STK11 loss as a predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.017, 95% CI -0.013 to 0.048; the point estimate is small, imprecise, and crosses zero. No validation request is made because the remaining voluntary independent-validation budget is zero. Overall, this appraise supports context-specific extensions of PTEN-STAT3 as within-dataset associations, confirms core accepted dependencies in additional contexts, and rejects the ARID1A-SMARCA2 paralog hypothesis plus the new MYC and STK11 STAT3 hypotheses.

Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: +0.119, CI 0.083 to 0.155, R96, validated +0.153, CI 0.097 to 0.209, R105; although smaller than the first four, it is precise, replicated, and biologically interpretable. MTAP loss, STK11 loss, RB1 loss, APC mutation, SMAD4 loss, NF1 loss, ARID1A loss, and PIK3CA mutation are generally null, negligible, direction-inconsistent, or too imprecise R45, R46, R145, R90, R91, R63, R288, R104, R241, R240, R251, R219, R220, R24, R250, R281, R216, R217, R218, R243. The constructed research markers D, E, and F show no meaningful main effects or modifiers R56, R57, R58, R53, R54, R55. Most interaction analyses are null, including modifications by lineage, library, culture, Cas9, growth rate, media, mutation burden, and screen quality for the core associations. The latest ARID1A paralog hypothesis is rejected R281, as are MYC and STK11 predictions of STAT3 dependency R287, R288. Confirmatory context analyses support accepted core effects but do not change the causal interpretation R282, R283, R284, R285, R286.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. These are associations within one lung-lineage CRISPR dataset and cannot establish gene dependency biology, causality, or external generalizability. Technical and biological confounding remains possible: library, Cas9 activity, screen quality, media, batch, growth rate, correlated genomic lesions, copy-number changes, mutation burden, aneuploidy, lineage subtype, and pathway state. I prioritize: (1) four refinements of the internally supported PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association in PIK3CA-mutant and TP53-mutant genomic contexts, with high aneuploidy as an interaction, and with high IFN-gamma signature as a cell-state subgroup; (2) the paralog-specific hypothesis that ARID1A loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency when SMARCA4 is intact; (3) context checks of accepted core associations, including TP53-loss/USP7 dependency among KEAP1-loss cells, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency among TP53-loss cells, MSI-high/WRN dependency among fast-growing cells, CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 dependency among STK11-loss cells, and SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency among high-stemness cells; and (4) two novel STAT3-dependency predictors, MYC amplification and STK11 loss. These analyses remain within-dataset association tests and will be interpreted for magnitude, precision, and consistency with the prior ledger rather than as causal or externally generalizable conclusions.","appraise":"I interpreted all returned estimates as already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1 mean-difference claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative, stronger dependency score; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative, weaker dependency score; for interaction claims, a positive signed estimate means the registered exposed-minus-comparator contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement. H268 accepts as a within-dataset PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association in PIK3CA-mutant cells: the signed difference is +0.261, 95% CI 0.118 to 0.403, with 36 exposed and 273 comparator cells. The effect is large relative to the STAT3 dependency distribution, but the exposed cell count is modest and the subgroup was tested after selection on PIK3CA state, so I keep it deferred rather than closed because PTEN-STAT3 remains discovery-only and may be confounded by PI3K-pathway and genomic context. H269 similarly accepts a PTEN-loss/STAT3 association among TP53-loss cells: +0.198, 95% CI 0.089 to 0.307, n 52/309. This is somewhat smaller than the main PTEN effect but still imprecisely positive and biologically plausible; it remains deferred as an unvalidated within-dataset context check. H270 rejects the claim of a positive high-aneuploidy interaction modifying PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency: the signed interaction is -0.089, 95% CI -0.215 to 0.037. The point estimate is opposite the registered direction and the interval is too wide to support a meaningful positive interaction. This is not a claim that high aneuploidy has no effect; rather, this dataset provides no evidence for the specific claimed positive modification. H271 accepts a large PTEN-loss/STAT3 association in high IFN-gamma signature cells: +0.458, 95% CI 0.345 to 0.570, n 59/384. The magnitude is much larger than the overall PTEN-STAT3 effect and the interval excludes zero comfortably. However, the subgroup was defined by a continuous assay and PTEN loss may co-occur with inflammatory or lineage states, so I accept it as an internally supported but deferred context finding, not a causal or generalized result. H272 rejects ARID1A-loss association with SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-intact cells: +0.002, 95% CI -0.021 to 0.026. This is essentially null and inconsistent with the paralog-compensation hypothesis. H273-H277 are accepted as confirmatory context checks of previously supported core associations. H273 shows TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency among KEAP1-loss cells: +0.791, 95% CI 0.750 to 0.832, n 74/276. H274 shows KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency among TP53-loss cells: +0.828, 95% CI 0.778 to 0.878, n 74/287. H275 shows MSI-high cells have stronger WRN dependency among faster-growing cells: +0.776, 95% CI 0.733 to 0.820, n 58/719. H276 shows CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency among STK11-loss cells: +0.111, 95% CI 0.038 to 0.184, n 63/276; the interval is less expansive than the main validated CDKN2A-MDM2 effect but remains positive and consistent. H277 shows SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in high-stemness cells: +0.789, 95% CI 0.749 to 0.830, n 91/362. These effects are large, precise, and consistent with earlier accepted and validated findings, though they remain associations within overlapping discovery samples. H278 rejects MYC amplification as a predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency: -0.008, 95% CI -0.040 to 0.025, with a null-to-negligible signed effect. H279 rejects STK11 loss as a predictor of stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.017, 95% CI -0.013 to 0.048; the point estimate is small, imprecise, and crosses zero. No validation request is made because the remaining voluntary independent-validation budget is zero. Overall, this appraise supports context-specific extensions of PTEN-STAT3 as within-dataset associations, confirms core accepted dependencies in additional contexts, and rejects the ARID1A-SMARCA2 paralog hypothesis plus the new MYC and STK11 STAT3 hypotheses.","synthesize":"No controller assessments are due and no new independent validation was released; I therefore make no assessment changes. All conclusions are within-dataset associations in the supplied 2000 lung CRISPR-screen dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims. Returned estimates are signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group has a more negative, stronger dependency score; for direction +1, a positive signed mean difference means the exposed group has a less negative, weaker dependency score; for interactions, a positive signed estimate means the registered exposed-minus-comparator contrast is stronger in the named subgroup than in the complement. The 10% relative benchmark is not directly meaningful on a negative-centered dependency scale, so I judged importance using effect magnitude relative to the dependency-score distribution and interval precision.\n\nSupported findings. Six associations are supported. First, MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency: signed mean difference +0.790, 95% CI 0.760 to 0.820, R11, with independent validation +0.797, CI 0.744 to 0.850, R26. This is robust across lineage, library, culture, Cas9 activity, mutation burden, aneuploidy, screen quality, growth rate, and media contexts. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency: +0.782, CI 0.761 to 0.802, R12, validated +0.805, CI 0.775 to 0.836, R39, and replicated across many contexts including ARID1A state, lineage, library, culture, Cas9, media, mutation burden, aneuploidy, screen quality, EMT, and stemness. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency: +0.797, CI 0.776 to 0.819, R7, validated +0.804, CI 0.773 to 0.835, R65. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with markedly weaker USP7 dependency: +0.804, CI 0.783 to 0.825, R38, validated +0.800, CI 0.768 to 0.831, R52. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: +0.119, CI 0.083 to 0.155, R96, validated +0.153, CI 0.097 to 0.209, R105; although smaller than the first four, it is precise, replicated, and biologically interpretable. Sixth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.269, CI 0.214 to 0.325, R239, with internal consistency in PIK3CA-intact R246, adenocarcinoma R249, PIK3CA- and TP53-intact R266, canonical-driver-intact R267, and screen-quality strata R271 and R272. The latest context analyses extend this discovery-only PTEN-STAT3 association to PIK3CA-mutant cells R277, TP53-loss cells R278, and high IFN-gamma signature cells R280, while formal interactions modifying the effect by PIK3CA, TP53, lineage, or high aneuploidy are not supported R268, R269, R270, R279. The six active claims H280-H285 are pre-specified within-dataset robustness checks of the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association. record.narrative: No validation request is made because the independent-validation budget is exhausted. I interpreted all estimates as already signed to the registered direction. For H280-H285, direction -1 means a positive signed mean difference indicates that PTEN-loss cells have a more negative, stronger STAT3 dependency score than PTEN-intact cells in the named context. H280, low IFN-gamma signature, shows a clear positive effect, +0.209, 95% CI 0.133 to 0.285, with adequate cells, so I accept it as a within-dataset consistency finding; it does not prove causality or generalizability and may reflect confounding between PTEN loss, IFN state, PI3K pathway state, or other genomic features. H281, high aneuploidy, also supports the effect, +0.201, 95% CI 0.092 to 0.310; this is somewhat wider and consistent with less precise estimation, but the interval excludes zero. This should not be confused with an interaction claim, because H270 did not support stronger PTEN effect specifically versus lower-aneuploidy cells. H282 and H283 accept low- and high-serum contexts: +0.239, CI 0.157 to 0.320, and +0.291, CI 0.216 to 0.366, respectively. These support media-context internal consistency but not causal media effects. H284, batch_a, gives +0.212, CI 0.097 to 0.326, which is positive but less precise; it supports presence of the effect in one technical batch without establishing batch causality or ruling out batch correlation. H285, high mutation burden, gives +0.277, CI 0.184 to 0.370, again internally supportive. Taken together, H280-H285 increase confidence in the PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association within this dataset, especially because the main accepted PTEN-STAT3 contrast remains internally coherent across many technical and biological strata. However, these are still discovery subgroup contrasts with multiplicity and correlated predictors, and PTEN-STAT3 remains the only accepted main association lacking independent validation. For H50, the MTAP-loss interaction on MDM2 dependency by TP53 loss is +0.030, 95% CI -0.039 to 0.0999. This is directionally positive but not statistically supported; the interval includes zero and remains wide enough that a small-to-moderate positive interaction cannot be cleanly excluded. Therefore I leave H50 unresolved rather than rejecting a positive modification, but close it for this dataset because the prior TP53-loss MDM2 main effect was itself null and no validation budget remains.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
No independent validation was newly released in this synthesis, no validation request remains, and no controller assessments were due. I therefore did not need to reassess due claims. I did correct two legacy direction-labeling errors: H75 is rejected because the CDKN2A-loss contrast for MDM2 dependency is negative, not positive, so the weaker-dependency direction is unsupported; the supported CDKN2A-loss association is H120, which states stronger MDM2 dependency. H104 is rejected because the BRCA2-loss SMARCA2 discovery contrast was imprecise and the independent validation did not reproduce it; the supported paralog association is SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency in H12. The deferred PTEN-loss STAT3 context checks were closed as accepted within-dataset consistency supports because the run is complete and validation budget is exhausted.

The final conclusions are associations within the supplied 2000 lung adenocarcinoma-dominated CRISPR-screen dataset. They are not causal effects, not proof of mechanism, and not guaranteed to generalize beyond this dataset. Returned estimates are signed to the registered direction: for direction -1, a positive signed mean difference means exposed cells have more negative, stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed mean difference means exposed cells have less negative, weaker dependency. The operational 10% relative-difference rule is awkward on a negative-centered dependency scale, so importance was judged by absolute difference relative to the outcome distribution and interval precision.

Supported within-dataset findings. Six associations are supported. First, MSI-high cells have markedly stronger WRN dependency: signed +0.790, 95% CI 0.760 to 0.820 (R11), validated at +0.797, 0.744 to 0.850 (R26). This effect is large relative to WRN-score variation and replicated across lineage, library, culture, Cas9 activity, mutation burden, aneuploidy, screen quality, growth rate, media, and batch-related strata. Second, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency: +0.782, 0.761 to 0.802 (R12), validated at +0.805, 0.775 to 0.836 (R39), and consistent in ARID1A-intact and ARID1A-loss contexts, lineage, library, culture, Cas9 activity, media, mutation burden, aneuploidy, screen quality, EMT, and stemness strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency: +0.797, 0.776 to 0.819 (R7 on the accepted direction claim H13), validated at +0.804, 0.773 to 0.835 (R65), with consistent subgroup support. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with markedly weaker USP7 dependency: +0.804, 0.783 to 0.825 (R38), validated at +0.800, 0.768 to 0.831 (R52), and consistent across many technical and biological strata. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: +0.119, 0.083 to 0.155 (R96 on H120), validated at +0.153, 0.097 to 0.209 (R105). This effect is smaller than the first four but is precise, replicated, and biologically interpretable. Sixth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.269, 0.214 to 0.325 (R239). This is the only main accepted association lacking independent validation. It is internally coherent across many strata, including PIK3CA-intact cells (R246), adenocarcinoma (R249), PIK3CA- and TP53-intact cells (R266), canonical driver-intact cells (R267), high and low screen-quality strata (R271, R272), PIK3CA-mutant cells (R277), TP53-loss cells (R278), high IFN-gamma signature (R280), low IFN-gamma signature (R289), high aneuploidy (R290), low serum (R291), high serum (R292), batch A (R293), and high mutation burden (R294). Formal interactions testing whether these features specifically modify the PTEN effect were not supported (for example R247, R248, R265, R268, R269, R270, R279). Thus the evidence supports a large, persistent within-dataset association, not evidence of effect modification, causality, or external validation.

Negative findings. Many biologically motivated driver-marker and pathway hypotheses are not supported. KRAS mutation does not support KRAS dependency (R1) or KRAS dependency in adenocarcinoma (R139), and KRAS-mutant effects on other dependencies are null or inconsistent. BRAF V600E does not support BRAF dependency (R3) or in driver-selected cells (R170). EGFR amplification showed a marginal discovery effect on EGFR dependency (R4), but independent validation contradicted it (R13), so the association is not supported. ERBB2 amplification does not support ERBB2 dependency (R6) or in driver-selected cells (R172), and related cross-driver effects are null or imprecise. MYC amplification does not support DHX9, POLR2A, USP7, KIF18A, MDM2, RPL11, or STAT3 dependency (R36, R9, R10, R48/R79, R238, R253, R287). BRCA2 loss is not supported for DHX9, POLR2A, WRN, KIF18A, or SMARCA2 dependency; the SMARCA2 signal was contradicted by validation (R94, R95, R82, R97, R83/R92). TP53 loss does not support MDM2, RPL11, POLR2A, WRN, or STAT3 dependency (R8, R37, R50, R84, R256), although it is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. KEAP1 loss does not support WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, MDM2, or STAT3 dependency (R70, R71, R25, R165, R255), apart from the accepted NFE2L2 association. PTEN loss does not support MDM2, WRN, SMARCA2, or NFE2L2 dependency (R242, R258, R259, R260), apart from the accepted STAT3 association. MTAP loss, STK11 loss, RB1 loss, APC mutation, SMAD4 loss, NF1 loss, ARID1A loss, and PIK3CA mutation are generally null, negligible, direction-inconsistent, or underpowered. The constructed research markers D, E, and F show no meaningful main effects or modifiers (R56, R57, R58, R53, R54, R55). Most interaction hypotheses are null or unsupported, including lineage, library, culture, Cas9 activity, media, growth rate, mutation burden, and screen-quality effect modification for the core associations. The WRN culture interaction was discovery-positive but validation-null (R59, R78).

Unresolved uncertainty. The largest unresolved scientific issue is PTEN-STAT3: it is large and internally robust but lacks independent validation, and PTEN loss may be correlated with PI3K signaling, IFN state, lineage, copy-number context, mutation burden, or other genomic features. CDKN2A-MDM2 is validated as a main effect but cannot be cleanly separated from 9p21 deletion, MTAP co-deletion, or TP53 state using available subgroup contrasts. Rare-stratum analyses and some interactions remain unresolved because cell counts or intervals are insufficient. All findings remain observational associations in one dataset, with possible technical and biological confounding from library, Cas9 activity, screen quality, media, batch, growth rate, ploidy, aneuploidy, mutation burden, and correlated lesions. Multiplicity remains a concern, though the five independently validated core effects are very large, precise, and replicated.

Most informative next analysis. The highest-value next step is pre-specified external replication and causal perturbation in independent cohorts: WRN dependency in MSI-high versus MSS models; SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-null versus SMARCA4-intact models; NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-null versus KEAP1-intact models; USP7 dependency in TP53-null versus TP53-intact models; MDM2 dependency in CDKN2A-null versus CDKN2A-intact models; and STAT3 dependency in PTEN-null versus PTEN-intact models. For PTEN-STAT3, prioritize isogenic PTEN restoration, PI3K-AKT or STAT3 modulation, and a preregistered IFN-by-PTEN interaction test. For CDKN2A-MDM2, use isogenic or copy-number-matched controls to separate CDKN2A loss from 9p21 deletion and MTAP co-deletion. Use multivariable adjustment for library, Cas9, screen QC, media, batch, growth rate, lineage, mutation burden, ploidy, aneuploidy, 9p21 copy number, MTAP, TP53, CDKN2A, PTEN, PIK3CA, KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, KEAP1, SMARCA4, ARID1A, IFN state, stemness, and EMT.
